clue.text: Checking car travel round Ulster

indicators.note: the phrase for car travel goes round the abbreviation for Ulster, enclosing it

parts.note: driving a car is motoring
NI, Northern Ireland, is often loosely called Ulster

explanation.surface: Someone inspecting a car journey around Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitoring something is keeping a check on it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Gospel writer showing little polish

explanation.surface: An evangelist with a lacklustre shine.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew the evangelist is shortened to a familiar name; a surface with a dull, unglossy finish has little polish.

clue.text: Observed bill and daughter

parts.note: a bill is a poster or notice put up in public

explanation.surface: Someone spotted a poster and a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: To have observed something is to have spotted it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Go on! One story's not enough!

explanation.surface: An incredulous listener who also wants more tales.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a scoffing retort meaning 'I don't believe you', and read literally it is a request for a further tale.

clue.text: Rooted round as said spirit matured

indicators.note: these words tell us the phrase is to be spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: rum is a spirit and matured means aged, together sounding like the answer

explanation.surface: Someone poking about while a spirit was ageing in casks.
explanation.definitionFit: To rummage is to search untidily, like a pig rooting about.

clue.text: Find Henry in lovely little corner

indicators.note: the letter for Henry is placed inside the word for lovely

parts.note: nice means lovely or pleasant
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone finds a man called Henry in a charming nook.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a recess or alcove, a small corner set into a wall.

clue.text: Trendy headgear back in the states

parts.note: U stands for upper-class, fashionable or socially acceptable

indicators.note: the word for headgear is read from its end to its start

parts.note: a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: A fashionable hat is making a comeback in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trendy' as U is the British upper-class sense of acceptable. The definition reads as 'one found in the states'.
explanation.definitionFit: Utah is a member of the American union, one of the fifty states.

clue.text: Puzzle how to beat lightweight

parts.note: to tan someone's hide is to beat them
a gram is a very light unit of weight

explanation.surface: A puzzle about how to defeat a boxer in the lightweight division.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangram is a Chinese dissection puzzle of seven flat pieces.

clue.text: Boss determined to be wilful

parts.note: the boss is the head of an organisation
strong can mean resolute or determined, as in strong-willed

explanation.surface: A boss who is set on being obstinate.
explanation.definitionFit: A wilful person is obstinate and insists on their own way.

clue.text: Toddler gets a pound, but that's the lot

parts.note: a tot is a small child
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A small child is given a pound coin and told that's all they get.
explanation.definitionFit: The lot means everything, the whole amount.

clue.text: A comedian playing in Europe

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters are played about with and rearranged

explanation.surface: A stand-up performing at a venue somewhere in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is read as 'country in Europe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Macedonia, now North Macedonia, is a Balkan country on the European continent.

clue.text: He takes steps to instruct his charges

definitions.text: He takes steps to instruct his charges

parts.words: He takes steps to instruct his charges
parts.note: reads like a careful teacher acting on behalf of his pupils, but the steps are literal footwork he teaches

explanation.surface: A conscientious tutor acting to educate his wards.
explanation.definitionFit: This man teaches ballroom footwork to pupils, so he literally instructs others in steps.

clue.text: Fellow-soldier aids Mr Cameron, maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints that these letters could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: A fellow-soldier who acts as an aide to the former Prime Minister David Cameron.
explanation.walkthrough: David Cameron was UK Prime Minister 2010-16.
explanation.definitionFit: A comrade in arms is someone who has served alongside you in battle.

clue.text: Really good look expressly to find misleading information

indicators.note: expressly hints at the words being expressed, said aloud

parts.note: proper is slang for really good and a gander is British slang for a look, said together casually

explanation.surface: Someone looks really hard, deliberately, to uncover disinformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper' as slang for thorough and 'have a gander' for take a look are British colloquialisms.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased or misleading material spread to promote a cause.

clue.text: Embarrassed as socialist gets confronted

parts.note: red is a common term for a left-winger or socialist
to face someone is to confront them

explanation.surface: A left-winger is embarrassed at being challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: Being embarrassed makes one blush, the cheeks turning crimson.

clue.text: Not so light; not so bright

explanation.surface: A comparison of two things lacking brilliance.
explanation.definitionFit: Less light means darker or duller in illumination; less bright means more stupid, slower-witted.

clue.text: Took the chair, despite having shown earlier bias

parts.note: pre- is a prefix meaning before or earlier
having sided with someone is having shown bias towards them

explanation.surface: Someone chaired a meeting despite previous partiality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having shown ... bias' is SIDED; 'earlier' gives PRE, which goes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To preside is to act as chairperson of a meeting.

clue.text: Capital decoration for English couple in oz

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the word is written twice

parts.note: pom is Australian slang for an English person

explanation.surface: A city adornment for a pair of English people in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is read as 'Cap-ital', of a cap: a pompom is a decoration on a cap. 'in oz' (Australia) sets the slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A pompom is a woolly ball sewn on top of a hat as an ornament.

clue.text: Reasons why I have put in French words

indicators.note: the contracted form of I have is placed inside the French for words

parts.note: mots is French for words
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone explains why they have been using French vocabulary.
explanation.definitionFit: Motives are the underlying reasons behind actions.

clue.text: Arab guide sees parent in monster's clutches

indicators.note: the parent is held in the monster's grip, so placed inside its name

parts.note: a dragon is a mythical monster
ma is mother, a parent

explanation.surface: A guide in the desert witnesses a mother being seized by a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic- and Turkish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Most are moved by his fine playing

definitions.text: Most are moved by his fine playing

indicators.note: moved suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Most of the audience are touched by a virtuoso's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished musician whose fine performance stirs listeners.

clue.text: If you receive this, you'll understand

definitions.text: If you receive this, you'll understand

parts.words: If you receive this, you'll understand
parts.note: literally receiving a communication, and idiomatically grasping the point

explanation.surface: A note promising clarity once it reaches you.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp what is meant is to catch on, and literally it is receiving a communication.

clue.text: I entered warren carrying cereal

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the word for a warren

parts.note: a warren is a labyrinth of passages, a maze

explanation.surface: Someone went into a rabbit warren with grain in their arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize is corn, a cereal crop.

clue.text: Humble yet miserly

explanation.surface: A person both lowly and stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean can describe lowly origins or poor quality, and also stinginess with money.

clue.text: Don't bother about mervin and Ned

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says to forget about two men called Mervin and Ned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase dismisses a matter, telling someone not to worry about it.

clue.text: In the past it helped the church survive

definitions.text: In the past it helped the church survive

indicators.note: the answer lies inside the run of letters spanning these clue words

explanation.surface: A historical note on how the church was sustained.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the definition and the wordplay: the letters sit across the boundary of 'past it helped'.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a tenth of produce or income paid to support the church and clergy.

clue.text: Included in gore's circle as well

parts.note: Al Gore, the US Vice President, gives Al's when possessive
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Something included in Al Gore's inner circle too.
explanation.walkthrough: Here the possessive 's is part of the letters: Al's. 'Included in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Also means too or in addition.

clue.text: Look in after offer is undercut

indicators.note: the words look in come after the word for offer

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in a bid
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone visits after a bid has been undersold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undercut' looks like a verb about pricing; it is the noun, the underside cut of a sirloin.
explanation.definitionFit: The fillet or tenderloin is the cut of beef from beneath the sirloin, called the undercut in Britain.
